content:
Requirement R15 (input): Input Search Pattern. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to define a search pattern for sensor/UAV coverage..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-15.1, F-15.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-15.<F>.1, Be-15.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-15.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent restated:** R15 lets the pilot define a search pattern that governs how the UAV/sensor covers a region — the shape/geometry of the coverage sweep — via Touch and Keyboard.

## Function candidates

**F-15.1 — Geometric coverage-area definition.**
The HMI's purpose is to let the pilot specify *where* and *over what extent* the UAV searches: define an area/region and have the sensor coverage derived from it. Goal = translate a spatial region into a search assignment.

**F-15.2 — Parametric pattern specification.**
The HMI's purpose is to let the pilot select and dimension a *named pattern type* (e.g. raster/ladder, spiral, sector) with its defining parameters (leg spacing, orientation, extent). Goal = pick a pattern archetype and set its numeric parameters — pattern-centric, not area-centric.

**F-15.3 — Search-tasking authoring & dispatch.**
The HMI's purpose is to produce a validated, transmittable search-pattern command the UAV can execute — the artefact exists to author a complete, envelope-valid tasking object and commit it. Goal = yield a correct dispatchable command, independent of how the shape is expressed.

These are genuinely distinct goals: F-15.1 is spatial/area-first, F-15.2 is pattern-type/parameter-first, F-15.3 is command-production/validity-first.

**Recommendation:** F-15.2. It matches the use case (6.3 "defines a new search pattern"), fits both fixed modalities cleanly (Touch to pick a pattern, Keyboard to dimension it), and stays distinct from R14 (aim-point designation, already spatial/gaze). F-15.1 risks overlapping R14's map-designation territory; F-15.3 is really the validation/dispatch layer that other requirements (R05, R07, R11) already established as a reusable pattern rather than a new function.

Which function do you want to close on?

**F-15.2 — Parametric pattern specification** closed.

Now Behaviour. One pathway per fixed modality, plus Mixed if it adds real value.

**Be-15.2.1 — Touch-only.**
Pilot taps a pattern-type tile (raster / spiral / sector) from a WAD palette. Selected pattern renders a live preview overlay on the map with draggable handles: drag to set orientation, drag edge handles to set extent, drag a spacing slider for leg separation. All parameters set by direct manipulation; TDC cursor is the throttle-resident equivalent for the same handles. Confirm via on-screen CONFIRM. Numeric values shown read-only as you drag.

**Be-15.2.2 — Keyboard-only.**
Pilot steps through pattern-type via bezel OSS (or rotary to cycle types), then enters each parameter as an explicit value — leg spacing, orientation (heading °), extent (length/width or radius) — on the UCP alphanumeric keypad / rotary encoders. Field focus advances by OSS. CONFIRM via bezel OSS. No pointing required — fully hands-on-panel.

**Be-15.2.3 — Mixed.**
Adds real value: pilot taps the pattern tile and coarse-drags extent/orientation on the map for fast spatial framing, then keys exact numeric values (spacing, heading) on UCP for precision the drag can't give. Preview updates from whichever input touched a field last; single shared validation gate before CONFIRM. This is the realistic cockpit path — fast spatial + precise numeric — but per the redundancy rule it must remain optional, not required.

**Recommendation:** All three, with **Be-15.2.1** and **Be-15.2.2** as the two mandatory modality-complete paths and **Be-15.2.3** as the value-add mixed path. This satisfies modality-complete redundancy (each fixed modality alone completes the full task) while capturing the genuinely better real-world workflow.

Note on sharing: the pattern preview overlay and shared validation gate could be shared with R14's map-designation surface (same WAD map, same confirm-gate idiom) — flag for consolidation, not duplicated here.

Which behaviour(s) to close on?

All three closed: **Be-15.2.1 (Touch-only)**, **Be-15.2.2 (Keyboard-only)**, **Be-15.2.3 (Mixed)**.

Now Structure. 2–3 concrete element sets that implement all three pathways together (the redundancy rule means one structure must serve all three).

**S-15.2.*.1 — Map-anchored pattern editor overlay.**
- WAD map overlay: pattern-type **palette tiles** (raster / spiral / sector) — Touch-select, or bezel-OSS cycle.
- **Live preview geometry** on the map with drag handles (orientation, extent, spacing) — Touch/TDC direct manipulation.
- **Numeric readout badges** on each handle, editable: tap-to-focus opens UCP entry, or select-field-by-OSS + UCP/rotary keying.
- Single **validation gate** (leg-spacing/turn-radius/area-vs-UAV-envelope) → shared **CONFIRM** (on-screen or bezel OSS).
- Reuses R14's map surface + confirm-gate idiom.

**S-15.2.*.2 — Docked parametric form panel (no map dependency).**
- Dedicated WAD **PATTERN panel** cloned from R11's UAV PARAMS layout: pattern-type selector row + numeric fields (spacing, heading, extent).
- Every field is multi-input: touch keypad, bezel OSS focus-step, UCP/rotary keying.
- Small **non-interactive schematic thumbnail** of the pattern (not a map) updates as values change.
- Same validation gate + dual-input CONFIRM.
- Strong reuse of the R01/R11 panel family; Keyboard-only path is cleanest here.

**S-15.2.*.3 — Hybrid: docked form + map preview link.**
- Combines the two: the S-.2 docked PATTERN panel drives numeric precision, linked live to an S-.1 map preview overlay for spatial framing.
- Either surface edits the same pattern object; whichever was last touched updates the other.
- Best fit for Be-15.2.3 Mixed, but heavier on WAD real-estate and cross-surface sync logic.

**Recommendation:** **S-15.2.*.3**. It's the natural home for all three behaviours — the docked form gives Keyboard-only its clean panel (Be-15.2.2), the map overlay gives Touch-only its direct manipulation (Be-15.2.1), and the live link between them *is* the Mixed path (Be-15.2.3) without extra machinery. It reuses R11's panel family and R14's map/confirm surface, so the cross-surface sync is the only genuinely new cost. If WAD space is tight, fall back to S-.1 alone (map-anchored, badges carry numeric entry) which still serves all three but makes Keyboard-only more cramped.

Which structure to close on?

**S-15.2.\*.3 — Hybrid docked form + linked map preview** closed.

## R15 summary
- **F-15.2** — Parametric pattern specification (select pattern archetype + set defining numeric parameters).
- **Be-15.2.1** Touch-only (palette tile + map drag-handles/TDC) · **Be-15.2.2** Keyboard-only (OSS type-cycle + UCP/rotary value entry) · **Be-15.2.3** Mixed (coarse spatial drag + precise numeric keying, shared gate).
- **S-15.2.\*.3** — Hybrid: R11-family docked PATTERN panel (numeric precision) linked live to an R14-surface map preview overlay (spatial framing), both editing one shared pattern object, single validation gate + dual-input CONFIRM.

**Reuse flags for consolidation:** R11/R01 panel family (PATTERN panel), R14 map surface + confirm-gate idiom, shared validation-gate pattern (R05/R07/R11).

R15 is fully specified across all three layers. Ready to close the requirement, or revisit any layer.
